claims.text: Conventional high-thermal-load metallic additive-manufacturing regimes generate residual thermal stresses.
Conventional high-thermal-load metallic additive-manufacturing regimes degrade mechanical properties.
Conventional high-thermal-load metallic additive-manufacturing regimes entail processing complexity.
Powder-loaded 3D ink-extrusion printing is feasible for producing multi-principal-element metallic alloys.
Powder-loaded 3D ink-extrusion printing can overcome the stated residual-stress, mechanical-property, and processing-complexity problems for AlCrFeNiSi feedstock.
The applicable printing condition is room temperature.
The process uses layer-by-layer ink extrusion.
Ink-extrusion printing refines the microstructure of AlCrFeNiSi.
Ink-extrusion printing makes the AlCrFeNiSi microstructure more homogeneous.
The ink-extrusion route cools more slowly than conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
Slower cooling reduces residual thermal stresses in printed AlCrFeNiSi.
More controlled microstructure formation improves the mechanical properties of printed AlCrFeNiSi.
Ink-extruded AlCrFeNiSi components will have better mechanical properties than components made under conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions.
Ink-extruded AlCrFeNiSi components will have lower residual thermal stresses than the conventional baseline.
Ink extrusion will make processing AlCrFeNiSi components simpler than conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
Optimal processing parameters and scalability of the proposed AlCrFeNiSi route remain uncertain.
